The crop-level figure moves to the RECOMMENDED rootstock (M26, the same basis PLA-465 used for mature_height_ft [10,14]). Page: ncsu_ext_handbook_tree_fruit (NCSU Extension Gardener Handbook ch. 15, already cited by apple) Table 15-4 'Recommended planting distances for apple trees grown on size-controlling rootstocks', Distance Between Trees (feet), NONSPUR column: Seedling 18-25, MM.111 14-18, MM.106 12-16, M.7a 10-14, M.26 8-12, Mark 4-8, M.9 4-8. -> in_row [96,144] (M.26), row not_authored: UGA C740 (uga_ext, cited) carries 'Table 2. Suggested Tree Spacing' with a Between Rows column per rootstock ('M 26 10 16 not recommended'), but its cached columns flatten ambiguously (non-spur / spur headers), so no row figure is read from it; per-rootstock row spacing is not modeled either (§5.1). WHY NCSU over UMN's class figures (standard 20-25 / semi-dwarf 12-15 / dwarf 6-8 ft, the spec's draft basis): (a) NCSU names each of apple's five rootstock rows, so no class-to-name mapping is needed; (b) UMN's own page calls M.26 'This dwarfing rootstock produces a tree 8-10 feet in height' (as do Clemson and UGA C740), so mapping M26 to UMN's SEMI-DWARF 12-15 ft would contradict the page it cites (UMN's own honest mapping would be its dwarf 6-8 ft class); (c) the MM106/MM111 decision row (§5.1) resolves itself: NCSU 12-16 and 14-18 ft sit around their 15/18 ft spreads. Nonspur is the column used because the rows describe rootstocks, not spur strains; spur strains make trees 60-70% as large (NCSU's Table 15-3 text; footnote a only lists spur cultivars). Overrides from the same table: M9 [48,96], M26 null (it is the basis), MM106 [144,192], MM111 [168,216], seedling [216,300]. The 4 scanner hits are pollinizer distance (50 ft) and fruit thinning (6 in): agrees.
